utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, very much, Madam Registrar. Before we will resume the cross-examination of the expert witness Tabeau, the Chamber still owes the parties a few decisions. The first decision is about, I would say, those documents tendered in relation to the testimony of Mr. Karavelic. Where first Prosecution document 3728, 26 maps they are admitted into evidence, but the witness only testified in respect of the confrontation lines marked on these maps. The Chamber will ignore any of the other markings on the maps, markings that were not made by the witness itself and were not the subject of his testimony. The Chamber is fully aware that it was a consequence of a decision made by the Chamber itself. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in relation to the shelling maps at least --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- There will be further evidence from Mr. Hadzic as to the manner of marking on the maps of the relevant positions in respect of the shelling impact sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine that at a later stage, that the restrictions and the views might be changed, if another witness testifies about other markings, either made by himself. I cannot, of course, foresee what will happen. But as it stands now, this part of the evidence is excluded. So only about the confrontation lines, because that was what the testimony of Mr. Karavelic was about. Mr. Ierace, you -- I wanted to pay attention to document P3727 which is the five maps, and I think your observations were about these five maps. The same limitations, the same restrictions are true for these five maps that are admitted into evidence. Then we have the document tendered by the Defence, D143, that is the letter about Mr. Karavelic not having been detained. It is admitted into evidence. The Chamber is confronted with the testimony of a witness who has given evidence in respect of detention, detention he was kept in. The Defence has challenged the reliability of the witness in this respect and has produced this document D143, while the Prosecution has tendered a document in support of the testimony about the detention. The Chamber is of the opinion that both documents are of a type that could assist the Chamber in making the determinations the Chamber will have to make. Of course, even if admitted into evidence, also document D143, the Chamber will still have to attribute the appropriate way to these documents and, of course, we will consider carefully any limits of the contents of the documents itself. Then we still have two translations into English which were not finally admitted into evidence, although we heard from the Defence that apart from the one small added part on the top of document, and would you please assist me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That there was no other objection as far as the translation is concerned. The Chamber takes proper notice of this -- of this minor point of incorrect or incomplete translation and admits the document into evidence. Then, this would also mean that P3736, which is a very small handwritten document which says that all the personal effects have been returned to Mr. Karavelic, with the exception of a sum of money, is also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I refer to these documents on both numbers, I should have added "point one," because that is the number for the translation. Then I have one observation to make in respect of the 92 bis statement the parties have still not yet received. The Chamber is working hard on it. But the Chamber does understand that the Prosecution specifically might not know all the reasons why the motion was rejected in some respect. And I especially ask the attention of the Prosecution for the reason why the motion was rejected in the respect of the witness Arifagic because the Prosecution has expressed its intention to call her. Once you have received the decision, you will read that the witness Arifagic, the statement of the witness is sought to be admitted because of the authentication of 15 documents. The statement will not be admitted into evidence because the Chamber is of the opinion that there is no need to receive any further evidence on these 15 documents that have already been admitted into evidence. In respect of two of these documents that were provisionally admitted on the 9th of January, the Chamber has addressed the Defence and has said that if there were any further objections against these documents, among these documents, the two I just mentioned, that further objections should be made that day and we have not heard since then from the Defence. So, therefore, the Chamber takes it that the provisional admission is now a final decision. I am mentioning it specifically because of the arrangements the Prosecution might have been prepared for the -- for calling the witness Arifagic. Then, a few other issues. The Defence indicated that by last Friday they would give further details about case presentation and numbers of witnesses. The Chamber has not received any further information, at least I have not seen anything by now. I just have a global number, but that is -- has it been submitted in writing, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. If the Chamber permits, perhaps today, at the end of the day, I can give you our schedule. If it's necessary, I can also tell you about it now, in general lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just trying to establish where there was still things that we had to pay attention to. So this is one of them and I do understand that the Defence is ready to give further information to the Chamber. There is another issue where the Chamber has put a question to the witness -- to the Defence and where we would expect an answer, an answer that should be given in closed session. I don't think it is necessary to turn into closed session now, but it was a question that was put to Defence last Friday. If there would be an answer, please indicate so that we can then turn into closed session and hear that answer. The last issue, and I apologise that I forgot to pay proper attention to it yesterday at the end of the session, that is the Defence would still indicate how much time they would still need for the further cross-examination of the expert witness Tabeau. Perhaps, if you would give us an indication of that last question. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Very briefly, we believe it will be just over an hour, but we would just like to say that, we would ask your Chamber to take into consideration the fact that this witness is nothing else but a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, does not wish or cannot give brief answers which is making us lose time. So basically, this is the Prosecution making the Defence lose time, which is why we will need just over an hour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The length of the answers given by an expert witness who testifies in this court and is employed by the Office of the Prosecutor is not the responsibility of the Prosecution in this case. When the witness, the expert witness, answers the questions, she is bound by the solemn declaration she gave and she has to behave fully independent of what her employer says. Would you be ready to resume the cross-examination, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, whatever you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before the witness comes back into the courtroom, might I clarify whether you will be at the end of the session requesting the Defence to update you on the number of witnesses and will you be dealing with other timetable issues, if so, I will be present at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think if the Defence is ready to give that information, we would love to hear and perhaps we can spend the last 15 minutes of today's court session to that. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the expert witness, Tabeau into the courtroom. [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Tabeau. Welcome in this courtroom again. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you give yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Having said this, the Defence will continue to cross-examine you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before the Defence continues, may I ask that she can be given the report and the annexes, the hard copy of the lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that would be P3730A and just the report itself, P3731.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3731B, as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you this morning go to the office or the premises of the Office of the Prosecutor, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my office where I usually work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to my own office, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. Did you speak to anybody from the Prosecutor's team? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You didn't say one or exchange one single word? You didn't utter a single word this morning, is that so?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke with a colleague of mine with whom I shared my room about matters that are related to our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you speak about this report with the colleague in a general fashion?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke about other projects that we have right now, and they were matters that needed to be discussed --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, please answer my question. I didn't ask you whether you spoke about other projects. I would be grateful if you could answer my questions, as long as you understand them, otherwise I will switch to another language. Did you speak about this project with the other worker?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So this is clear. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask you, if you would have carefully listened to the expert witness, you would have noted that when you interrupted her that she already gave the answer that she kindly repeated later on, on a specific question of you. May I ask you to follow the manners of courtesy which we owe to any other individual. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so, all the more gladly, since it is my rule too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Mrs. Tabeau, Katyn -- how many casualties? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Katyn: How many casualties?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Objection. That question is much too vague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How many casualties, what is that related to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please -- the witness does not understand the question as you formulated it. Would you please reformulate it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The Katyn forest, how many casualties?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am sorry. I didn't hear the last --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is about Katyn, this is a place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, did you want to ask the witness how many casualties occurred at a certain place, because I am following you in French and I had great difficulties in even following the words you expressed. But it seems that the witness understand your question, but could you please formulate them in such a way that everyone understands them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How many casualties or victims in the forest of Katyn. Do you understand what I am saying, Madam?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what you are saying. I don't know exact numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you tell you between 18 and 20.000 victims, are these accurate figures as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know exact figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Fine. I will move on to your expert document. Page 5 did you state this, I am going to quote in English [In English] "Vast majority of those killed or wounded were men, most of them were at active of military age [18-60] and were soldiers." [Interpretation] Is this is sentence of yours, Madam?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written -- read from the report from page 5 yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you mind answering with a yes or no. We would save time this way. Thank you. Reversely, and here I am referring back to page 102 in your report, is it true that women have, relatively speaking, suffered little during this period as victim?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this figure when you have referred to, relatively little.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you confirm for us and for the transcript that during the time taken under scrutiny, there were only 10 suicides?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to check this figure in the annex where it is reported. Yes, there were 10 suicide cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So this is for the two years or 24 months that you studied, is that so? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the period stated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you compare this suicide rate which is, to me, very low with the usual rate to be found generally in ordinary cities in Europe in normal situation; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before the witness proceeds to answer, the objection is not to the question itself, but it is to a comment which is introduced into the question as the opinions of counsel as to what is "high" or "low." I would respectfully submit that counsel at this time ought not to comment on what he -- what his own assessment is. That is not probative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but it is part of the question. If he would have not have said "to me," but if he would have said: "Did you compare this suicide rate and did you find them to be very low to the usual rate," then, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think you will get the answer. And whether you -- whether that is your opinion, is not, I think, of vital importance. So I would not -- I think it doesn't add anything to the question, that according to you, but you can ask the question, whether it is low or high. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I very gladly rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you compare suicide rates; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, you don't know whether this is a high or a low rate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is a low or high. But this is not a rate we are discussing. This is number, absolute number, 10 cases of suicide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for an expert witness, if an expert witness is of the opinion that the answer she gives, even being aware that if "yes" and a "no" would do, that if it would create confusion, if she could not clarify part of her answer, she will be allowed to do so. But, perhaps, Ms. Tabeau, if you address me and ask whether you can give a clarification, I will let you know whether the Chamber allows you to give a clarification. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, is it true that you did not seek to see, for the purpose of your expert report, the hospital admission books for various hospitals?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't use them in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know or did you not know how many admissions there were per year, generally speaking, in a period -- in a time of peace for a population of some 350.000 inhabitants? I only have in mind accidents here, of course.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't use this type of sources in this report. I cannot know. I didn't discuss them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You said that you didn't use them, which would not mean that you didn't know about them. I asked you whether you knew about them or not.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure that you asked your question whether I knew. It was -- let me find it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question was this as follows: Did you know?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that this type statistics exist and probably also for the war period existed to a certain extent. I also know that there were colleagues who were working with this type of statistics. It was not my domain, say, of research.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were these figures given to you or not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read at a certain moment the report that was made based on the sources, but I don't know the figures right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can exhibit D154 be submitted, be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please assist, Mr. Usher. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, please focus only on page 2 of the document. May I ask you this: Do you read or understand French, which is one of the official languages of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand French. Please, if you could translate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you read French?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know French.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. There is a table, it only deals with admissions for reason of accident which is ACC as an acronym, for the last three years. In a city of comparable size in Europe. So, another city than Sarajevo. In this case, this is Geneva, around 350.000 inhabitants. We have a figure of 18.697, for instance. Does this figure, to you, look normal or not? If you can't answer, just say so.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer. It is a different domain of research.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I state for the transcript that this document was recently sent to me by the general directorate of the Cantonal Hospitals in Geneva so this is a very authentic document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am moving on to another line of questioning. For the sake of your report, did you examine a document which is entitled [In English] "Sniper: September 3, 1992 until August 10th, 1994," [Interpretation], the reference number is 00986276A-6309. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you aware of the document?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Am I to understand that the Prosecutor did not give you this document for the sake of your report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier yesterday that we work -- I believe I said, we work quite independently. Demography is just a group which is doing demographics, and this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed. But I still haven't got an answer for my question. Did the Prosecutor give you this document or not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Mr. Usher help me. I want to show you a document, number 155, for the transcript. I am only interested in the first page, Mr. President. The document is much longer, but this is by way -- shown to the witness by way of an example. The first part of the document is only the translation of the top line or top lines, and as to the rest these are only names or dates or names of hospitals, therefore, not to be translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness you had enough time to look at the document. Did you see it before or not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know -- I remember there is a list of sniping casualties in -- attached with the indictment. But, I cannot say for sure that this list you gave me and the list attached to the indictment is the same thing. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Please go to the date of the 14th of September, for example. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you see that there is about 10 wounded on that date? This is in the last but one column.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I see only one name mentioned on this page. I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are referring to the 14th of September. There are two entries with the 14th of September. I take it that you are referring to the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, can you see that in one of the two entries. There are 10 names, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Good. Thank you. And by the way, there is only one for the 14th of September where there are wounded. The other people are dead.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: There could be no confusion.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have 10 names of wounded and 1 killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. I am talking about the wounded. Is it true or isn't it true that with relation to locations or places where the accidents took place, there is no indication whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. So, are we talking about snipers in the last column of the table?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, Madam Witness, don't you think it is surprising, out of 10 wounded people, therefore survivors, none of them is able to remember where they allegedly were wounded?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not surprising to me. If I would got wounded unexpected, I would probably not know where the shot come from, came from. This is a kind of shock that is by definition you cannot explain that people remember these type of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, when you are wounded, generally speaking, well, you are being taken to a hospital and there are other people who drive you there. Those people driving you are not wounded, and you still don't think it is surprising that we should know where these people were wounded?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the circumstances, so it is a question I cannot answer. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If I put this question to you, it is because, in your expert report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... two different questions to the witness. The first was whether it was surprising that injured person would not know where he was wounded. And the second was whether "we" would not know, and that creates a question, I have got no idea what is the source of the information. It says on the first line that it is "source" and you say it needs no further translation. I see different sources and I don't know whether this is what parents report to the school of their children or what the parents said or whatever it is, I have no idea. Could you perhaps first, especially since the sources for the 14th of the 9th are not the same apparently. Could you tell me and you say -- at least your question was that it wounded person would not have known where he was wounded, but what is "ZHMP"? Is that is list filled in by the wounded persons or is that a hospital register or is that a... I've got no idea. Would you please either ask this to the witness if she knows or give us some clarification in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could, but I don't think -- oh, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, do you know the sources that are listed in the first column on the left?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I only understand "Statisticki Zavod", which is statistical institute or institute for statistics. And I don't understand the other names, interpretations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Madam Witness, is it true that on this page, for the sake of the example, we can see a lot of entries, statistically speaking, where there are no indications regarding a location. I am talking about the second, the third, fifth, the sixth, the 8th, the 10th and the 11th and the 13th?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is indeed that these locations are not given --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are going to another series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have distributed a document, number 156, and then we are going to come back to another exhibit with the help of Mr. Usher. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, do you know the name of Mr. Nedzad Ajnadzic?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If I tell you that the Oslobodjenje newspaper said that in Sarajevo, the number of civilian victims was 15.000, does this seem to be a media exaggeration to you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is probably too much, too many.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now going to ask Mr. Usher to assist us with the distribution of another document bearing the number 157.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, could you please look at page 2 in this document. You have it before you. Can you read the number -- the reference number 00986276?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a document which comes from the Prosecution. Could you please tell me how many deaths as a result of -- or alleged deaths as a result of sniping for this period?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is 361 mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. What are your own figures, the ones that you were dealing with?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe we can check this in the report how many, but it is more than that, I believe. On page 68 in the annex, we can read that there were, in total, 699 casualties of sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Madam, so in the report it is -- the ratio in the report is double and we have a document from the Prosecution which says there were 361 victims and your report which roughly claims that it is double. So how is this possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I -- that is something that is outside of this witness's expertise. Unless the witness can be sure to know the source of this document and why it was disclosed and how we got this document and how it was prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you are asking, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for an explanation of the difference in numbers. That is what you are doing. If I would ask the witness an explanation for the difference in numbers of well, let's say, of 5 people riding bicycle on my street, compared to 30 people eating strawberries she might have some difficulty, because that is not the same. Could you please explain what this document is. I don't know whether the witness has had time to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. This document comes from the Prosecution and it tries to establish, according to the Prosecutor, gives us the numbers of civilian victims, sniper victims, of alleged sniper victims for the given period which is from the 10th of September 1992 until the 10th of August 1994. So we now have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please -- I see another number on that document. Can you explain what that is so we can all know exactly what the document is about. It says 870 cases of sniper action against civilian in the period mentioned. Could you indicate what that means and perhaps tell the witness before she answers your questions. Is this a case study of limited number of cases or is this all the sniper cases known during a certain period or is this to indicate that all the numbers together were 870? Well, there are a lot of possible explanations, but I see a number which is not part of your explanation to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know more about it myself, since this is a Prosecution document. So I cannot go through the chronology of the Prosecution documents. They are as they are given -- as they are handed over to me. So it is not up to me to find out about the figures. It is up to the Prosecution to give us the numbers. The Prosecution should give me their figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The figures given by the Prosecution is the figures which are testified to in court by this witness. Quite a lot of material has been disclosed to the Defence pursuant to the Rules, where it is relevant or pursuant to whichever rule of disclosure. They are not disclosed necessarily because they reflect the position of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wanted to add, but I was stopped by the Defence. The answer I gave, the answer 699 casualties of sniper was a total number of all casualties, civilians and soldiers. If we look next page at the table page 69, at the number for civilians, it is 253. This is table A3.8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are referring to your report, what page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 69, table A3.8. We have 253 civilians who were killed by sniper, which is a lower number than the number reported in this document that we have been discussing right now. But still both numbers are incomplete, as there is no complete source for this type of -- about this type of events. Both are samples or representations, estimates of the unknown total, I believe. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I have your leave to continue? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I would like you to do the same thing for the wounded now, looking at the document that you have before you. We have for the civilians 756 wounded.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And according to your findings, Madam Witness?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have on page 19, 1.296. Is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you talking about civilians?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am speaking about civilians, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that these are different figures?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are different figures. And I repeat, that both these figures are just approximations and incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Madam Witness, in order to save time, since time is running out, do we have the same type of difference which exists for the case of the shellings, and would you then give me the same type of answer for that difference as well?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I ask counsel to clarify that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, in general, Mr. Stamp, if the witness understands the question, we will hear her answer. If it is not clear to the witness, the witness will tell us, so I think -- so if you understand the question, would you please answer it. If not, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You didn't show me your figure or other figures, alternative figures related to shelling. But I think what is really confusing is mixing up different things. Well, we deal here with a very special situation. We have a conflict situation in which normal procedures for collecting statistical information don't work out. It is never possible during the conflict period to obtain statistical information about demographic events in the way they are normally -- these type of records are normally collected. So we have to base our conclusions on sources that are different than regular vital statistics, vital events registration. And every source is just a sample, incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very well possible that we will see a different figures related to the same phenomenon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam. Now, before we continue with this line of questioning, you said that your study was only related to six municipalities in Sarajevo. Were these, the municipalities, whole municipalities?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area within front lines, actually covered parts of six municipalities, not complete whole municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What are the municipalities which were not covered by your survey, by your study?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That were not covered by my study. It was, I think, Trnovo -- no, I can tell you what I covered by my study. Perhaps this is the simpler way of saying this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Sarajevo, Stari Grad, Novi Grad, Novo Sarajevo, Vogosca, Ilidza, and Centar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And Centar. Thank you. So which one of these municipalities was not studied in its entirety, as a whole?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think every of these municipalities, every one of these municipalities was studied only partly, as part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that for each of these municipalities, you were missing some data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, why?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is that the front lines actual split these municipalities in such a way that only part of these municipalities were included in the survey area. And part was left --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Therefore, Madam, if you are giving us the number of inhabitants about 340.000 inhabitants, do we agree in considering that this is just a part -- that this is just a part of these six municipalities that this is about?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, would you agree with me in considering that during these two years of war that we are looking at, all of the losses, all of the casualties that was suffered by the Sarajevo population, is probably lesser than a rate of 0,5 per cent per annum?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say I need clarification. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. The rate of losses, when we look at the population as a whole, the population of Sarajevo, is it true that this rate was lesser than 0,5 per cent per year?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible to check the rate per annum in 1991 because this is in the report and it is six municipalities, entire municipalities --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, no, Madam, I am going to interrupt you, Madam. No. During the two years of the war, 1992, 1994, the ones that we are focussing on, is it true that the rate of the losses suffered by the population, globally speaking, is it less than 0,5 per cent per year, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not lesser, it is higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you demonstrate this for us, please? What is the late of the losses?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is page 40 from the report in which we show rates of killed and all deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, Madam. You have this rate, you have 1153, so for how many years would that be, would that cover?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This rate is for two years, for the whole period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we divide that by two, how much would we get, then approximately?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is five per hundred, I believe, 5.000 per 100.000, so this is the rate you mentioned, I believe, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I said 0,5 per cent, is that the rate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it 5 per cent?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] 0,5 percent.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh yeah. I am sorry, I understood 5 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] And I said "0,5 per cent". [Interpretation] So, therefore, the question that I am asking per year is that correct, then? If we know that the Sarajevo population is large?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it would be 500 per 100.000, I believe. This is the rate you mentioned, right? So in the question you asked, is whether this rate, 500 per 100.000, is lesser than the rate we calculated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I simply asked you Madam, if yes or no, the rate of the losses that were suffered by Sarajevo was probably under 0,5 per cent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is the rate we obtained for the area within front lines. These rates are higher than rates you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, if we have 3.798 out of a population of about 340.000, this gives us a rate of 1,153 per cent, do we agree, generally speaking, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said 1,153 per cent, it is not correct. These are rates that are given for 100.000 population. If you express the rates by hundred, these are different values then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, Madam. What is the rate in percentages, could you please do it for us, on a population of 340.000, for 3.798 victims, total?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rate I included in table that is already now at the ELMO, on the ELMO is 1,153 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in terms of percentages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So if we divide this rate by 2 for each year, what would be that rate then? Be 0,5? Very well. So, what the figure I gave you, Madam expert, these figures were correct, do we agree on that, yes or no, Madam?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it is your approximation of the annual rate, these are correct figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So our figures are correct. Thank you. Since we are speaking of this, and in order to understand these figures well, Madam expert, is it true that there were four other municipalities, additional municipalities, that you did not take into consideration in your calculation; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were four municipalities that I excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So, I believe that you answered no to this question but still the names of those four municipalities, do you know them?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to think about it. It would be Ilijas, Trnovo -- I don't remember other two. Please mention the other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please look at page 19 of your expert report. And perhaps you will find the name of Hadzici and also Pale?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: These are the two names that we were looking for. Thank you. Madam Witness, I would like us to come back to your figures. You said earlier that in relation to the civilian population, there is a certain number of deaths which is part of -- was part of your findings. Could you please give us again this figure, the figure is civilian losses, and I believe that the figure amounted to 1.399 casualties or losses. Could you tell us if this is correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is table 1, page 3 -- sorry -- 4. This 1.399.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Madam, is it true that the rate of civilian victims, generally speaking, of those who died, was per year some 0,2 per cent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we are -- I would disagree because we didn't have information about the civilian population, so we couldn't calculate the rate. It is not that you may relate events from a certain group of the population to the whole population.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, I agree with you, but if we have, let's say, 1.400, let's take a round number, out of 340.000 inhabitants, divided by two years, wouldn't the result of that give us 0,2 per cent, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer the questions. It doesn't make sense to divide any two numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: For the Defence, it makes a lot of sense, to find out what was the percentage over a given population per year. If you can answer mathematically or algebraically, could you please give us an answer? Is it true that this calculation gives us in a percentage -- speaking in percentages, 0,2 per cent in annual losses, and I am talking about civilian population, allegedly civilian population?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... will bring a small calculator for your next question, before your next question. But believe me that calculating demographic rates is not a matter of dividing one number by another number. These are measures of intensity of a process. And in order to be correct, you really must relate events in the population that was exposed to risk of these events, not just any numbers, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. But Madam, the population was 340.000. So we know that there were 700 civilians killed per year which is 1.400 for two years. So could you please give us a rate, I have given you a rate which is 0,2 per cent. You don't want to confirm it or you can't confirm it, so I am going on to another question. Madam, I am talking about deaths, people who died, allegedly as a result of sniper activity. Is it true that you have kept as a figure, that you have a figure as 352 or 353 victims for these two years; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are speaking now about the rates or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about absolute numbers, figures.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about civilian victims, that is, allegedly civilians.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my table on page 69, I see 253.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Madam, could you do the same exercise if we, if we look at the population of 340.000 people, is it possible to take a rate of civilian victims, allegedly snipers victims the rate would be 0,037 per cent? The Defence is precise here.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, I must answer, it is the same problem here with the population at risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. For the transcript, Mr. President this is 0,037, so that things are clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And Madam, you cannot answer, is that it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree with the way you calculate rates. It is just the wrong way of doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, what happens at this moment that the Defence has indicated several times that what the Defence considers a relevant rate that is civilian casualties, whether or not caused by sniping, at the whole population makes sense. The expert witness says that from a demographic point of view, that it makes no sense to her. I did not hear any disagreement as the arithmetics are concerned. Did I understand your testimony well that you are not contesting the ability of the Defence to divide numbers by numbers, but that in your view, it gives no useful information? Well, of course, finally, whether this is useful or not, the Chamber is -- will have to determine whether it is useful or not. There is no disagreement about 4 divided by 2, it makes 2. There is disagreement about the Defence -- between the Defence and this expert witness who does not want to add to what the expert witness thinks is useless information. I think, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the positions are clear. Please, could you proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I would like us to go to your page 68, the page 68 of your expert report. You found it, Madam?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, the Chamber would like to know that what would be the proper way of establishing rates in this respect, because the witness has told us several times that this was not a proper way of doing it. What would have been the proper way, Ms. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The proper way would be to relate the events that were obtained or reported in our report for civilians, to the population of civilians and for soldiers to the population of soldiers. These are much smaller populations and the rate would be much higher than the rates presented by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you would say rates makes sense, if you relate civilian casualties to civilian population, and military casualties to military and that would be the proper way of doing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what the Defence proposed to you is to establish a rate between civilian casualties on the whole of the population --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the whole of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on this issue, I will have to ask the expert something else, because one of the questions related to the global population of Sarajevo that we knew about, because everyone says this is roughly 350.000 people and the first question was asked about the entirety of the losses in relation to the global population, that is civilian and military together, in relation to the population of Sarajevo. So the methodology was very much what the expert has indicated. And if my mathematical ability isn't much, I believe that I have established what you have asked about. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am going to come back to page 68 --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I add something with this regard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The population of 340.000 that we used in our population was not the population of the six municipalities. This is an estimate for the parts covered within front lines. We obtained this number from the number of questionnaires, from the survey, and applied certain statistics about average number of persons in one household in these municipalities to end with the total of this population. We also included approximately 7.000 displaced persons reported by UNHCR in Sarajevo. So this is our numbers. We actually were -- have done a lot of effort to use a proper -- the proper population in the calculation of our rates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please move to your next question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On page 68, Madam, a question of methodology here. You have here a presentation of causes of death and I can see that the first part of the report doesn't have a subheading, although the second part of the report here does have a subheading. Do you see it? It is a direct losses in relation to direct casualties of war.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we now have a problem with methodology as far as the Defence is concerned. Why do you have this heading "direct casualties of war." Shouldn't it be ahead in the first column, that is regarding the shelling and other firing, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is because the subheading that for your information and for the information of anyone in this court, we wanted to show which specific categories were included in the group, for instance, direct casualties of war. The subheadings are very small as every single one, categories. So it is -- it makes sense to combine them and show them as one group. This is why we created the category "direct casualties of war." And this category includes the subcategories as mentioned in the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. We did read this. But my question, that perhaps you didn't quite grasp, wasn't that one. I was asking why isn't this subheading at the head of the column? That is before firearms shelling, firearms sniping et cetera. Why isn't that, this heading, the first line?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: For firearms, you are suggesting that I should include a heading, general heading "firearms" as such?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, Madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand your question well, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you asked the expert witness to explain why she would not count firearm shelling, firearm sniper, firearm shooting, firearm other, under a heading which would be direct casualties of war? I mean, why are these categories not under the heading of direct casualties of war? Is that what you would like to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is even clearer than when I explained it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... clear answers, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Would you please answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is mistake I made that the other heading is direct casualties and not "other" direct casualties of war. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So I assume, Madam Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I believe the witness was in the process of giving an explanation to the court

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did your finish your answer? I do understand that you said it should have read "other" casualties of war. That was expressing that the first categories were also direct casualties of war but not the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that was your explanation, then please proceed. I don't know whether you intended to add something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may add, it was only that we tried to show the major causes of killing. Major means significant numbers should be shown for each category. The categories, shooting, firearms, are all unspecified because you see the numbers. And for direct casualties of war --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may interrupt you. I think it was mainly the matter of why you would not consider these categories to be direct casualties of war. And any further question was not put to you, but perhaps, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I am just taking note that this heading should be up and then the other one heading should be "other," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So if we go to page 5 of your report, Madam, could you please do that. You have found the page, Madam?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: At the very end of the paragraph called "absolute numbers of casualties", we have one of the dashes and I will read it in English [In English] "the analysis of timing also suggests that many civilian casualties were not caused by mechanisms which were killing or wounding soldiers thus some kind of targeting civilians might be possible." [Interpretation] Have you found this sentence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, my questions are the following: Where and when in your report were you able to compare what you call "the timing"? Could you please tell me. Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a section in the report that discusses the results of timing, as we call it, "timing." So this is in section -- it is section 5.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Page, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me where you compared the timing -- I can see the heading, but where did you do the comparison then?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is in the tables from 9 to 14, where we listed the dates with the highest numbers of casualties for civilians and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. That is clear. But, Madam, did you examine the locations of the events in relation to the timing; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, but not specifically. So I did not compare every single event --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- The dates --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Madam Witness, let us imagine that one day there is a combat left from the confrontation lines without much damage among the military, but there is a stray bullet, faulty fire, faulty firing which results in 10 civilian casualties which results to the right of the front line. Did you consider this possibility, yes or no, in your analysis of timing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The same question for the targets in the centre of the city. Were you given information on the entirety of targets in the centre of the city?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what you mean. But if you mean whether I received written information about targets, the city centre, I didn't have such information --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So, Madam Witness, we agree that including this reservation, not knowing where the target, military target was in the centre of the six municipalities you mentioned, you would not know if these victims were in relation, yes or no, to an attack on a legitimate target?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had general information about place or killing and wounding for both civilians and soldiers, but, well, I didn't compare this information with some other source that would be telling me about targets in the city centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me take a very clear example. You have 10 to 15 victims on the Benevolencija Street, I like the name of the street. These 10 to 15 victims, are they going to be taken up into your figures without any other processing of them?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, we process this information, we called "displace" as I said in local community, and then further as a municipality, and then we use this item in the analysis. We did not study places as streets or under common names, given as common names, very specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But specifically, this name of Benevolencija, doesn't mean anything to you, does it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you expect me to remember all streets in Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just interfere. Do I understand you well, and I am questioning yourself, why you don't ask the expert witness, whether she considered whether casualties, maybe civilian or soldiers, could be -- could have occurred because of the presence at a certain place of a military target that would justify an attack on that place? Is that the question you would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the question I generally put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It you are calculating, if you are analysing your figures, did you take into account that sometimes civilians might have been close to concentrations of military people, headquarters, troops, whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is clear now. I did not use additional information of this type in the analysis of the data from this survey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I look at the interpreters and see -- would this be your last two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These would be the Defence questions in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would then conclude the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I then have the cooperation of the booth for the last two questions, which include the very very last questions as well Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, can we now look at page 98 in your report. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So that everything is clear because in the chronology, it might not be stated there is a peak both among the civilians and the soldiers and, of course, for all wounded and on a date which is after the 30th of January 1994, if this is the case, can you please confirm that this is in keeping with the date of the 5th of February 1994, because the date of the 5th is not mentioned?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is 5th, the 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So we are talking about the Markale attack?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true, and we are talking in purely statistical terms, that there is a drastic drop in the number of victims, whoever they may be, straight after the date of the 5th of February, and this is true until the date which is of concern to us, of the 10th of August, 1994; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, if you know this please tell us: Is the situation, is it a causal situation that is then in place?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I believe there had been probably certain extraordinary events that caused this significant difference in the pattern of timing observed before the 5th of February and after the 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very last question. It is the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As far as you know, has any proceedings been launched or -- with relation to Katyn?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, questions should not only be understood by a witness, for example, because she has a certain personal background but should be informative for the Chamber as well and should be understandable for the other party as well. So would you please indicate -- I take it that you are referring to, well, let's say, occurrence outside the timeframe and outside the geographical frame of the indictment. So would you then please be clear, and it is not just the witness. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought it was clear for everybody. I am sorry. Mea maxima culpa. I am very sorry for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know, Madam Witness, whether some ad hoc proceedings were started following the massacre of 18.000 young officers who were executed through a bullet in their napes in NKVD at the time, I don't think so?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then adjourn until 25 minutes past 4.00. Could the Prosecution already indicate whether there is any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, just one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One or two questions, so shortly --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not literally one or two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but a limited number. Yes, I am trying to understand everyone, according to what they intend to say. We will adjourn for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I was informed that you wanted to address the Chamber, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very briefly, Mr. President. My co-counsel is more shocked, Ms. Pilipovic, than I am. We were unfortunately the target of something that I would call a verbal aggression in the halls, in the corridors, during the break. It was probably by someone who was earlier in the public gallery and who seemed not to appreciate us as defendant lawyers of Mr. Galic, nor Galic himself. Now, Mr. President, we didn't provoke this. We were just going in the corridor to have a coffee and we were attacked by a person we have never seen before. They provoked the Defence. There was -- this provoked a certain upset, as you can imagine. And now particularly, this shocked Ms. Pilipovic, although I have seen such occurrences. I believe that this is unbearable, unacceptable, and for once I remained quiet. And it was very hard for me to remain silent and not respond. And I am afraid I will not remain silent if this situation happens again. Could you please take note of what has happened. I don't think that we are the only ones who are subject to this. Now, thank you for allowing me to address you publicly on this subject, because I hope that in the future, such incidents are launched against whoever will not happen again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is a very serious matter. First of all, I would like to express my appreciation that you took Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. whatever effort not to give the person involved, of whom I do not know the identity, any opportunity to further escalate the, whether it was verbal, or at least the hostile attitude towards you. The Chamber will ask specific attention of the security for what happened and the Chamber will take care that the Registry will be informed. If, in your view, any specific measure should favour that this would not happen again, please let the Chamber know, since the security of the Defence is just as important as the security of everyone in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for your attention. Again, I am saying that security does a very good job, although sometimes they screen us very carefully, Defence lawyers, but obviously the security of Mr. Galic is not in question, is not at risk. The security of the Defence lawyers of General Galic is not at risk. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then I hope, Ms. Pilipovic, that you will recover from it. I can imagine, the Chamber can imagine what is difficult thing it is to experience, that if you are fulfilling your duty, if you are doing what Defence counsel should do, that you are approached in this way. Then, is the Prosecution ready to re-examine the witness? Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Tabeau, we had to deal with a procedural matter for a couple of minutes that caused the delay. Mr. Stamp, please proceed with the re-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You were shown page 102 of the report. In an answer to a question about the two graphs on that page you agreed that women have suffered relatively little during this period. When you say, "relatively," relative to what?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to men, of course. This figure, the one numbered A5K4, is a comparison of the mortality of killed -- rates of killed of men and women.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the course of cross-examination you said that every source, it is just a sample, it is incomplete. Can you explain what you mean by, "incomplete"?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incomplete means that not all actual events are included, are covered by the sources. Sources are not exhaustive, simply, these type of sources. Also our source, Household Survey, but these are still incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The fact that this is incomplete, what effect would that have on the figures that you have found?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is that from other sources it is likely, we would be able to collect more information about cases of killed individuals and the numbers presented in this report, presented here as at-least numbers, minimum numbers, would be even higher than what is on paper by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] This is in relation to what Mr. Piletta-Zanin said this is document 154, this is the document from Geneva. And the question is: What is the population of Geneva?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for this question. I am not an expert, as you know, but I can tell you that the population of Geneva is approximately 350.000 people. And to be perfectly honest, I have to say that when we look at the topographic situation which is very specific to Geneva University Hospital were made for a larger basis because the people from the border regions can have access. So, in fact, the figure goes up to 400.000 people, if we include the basin on the outside, because you know the Geneva is practically inside the French basin. So the population is roughly 350.000. Does this answer your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, but now I would like to have an explanation on the table that you presented. We have the first part under the same heading, 24 hours, and we have the same hospitals. I believe that the first one is referring to the admissions, hospital admissions, and then the other two out-patients.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I am sorry, I am going to try and explain as follows: There are two institutions which comprise the -- what we call the HUG, which are the University Hospitals of Geneva. These two institutions are the Cantonal Hospital and the second hospital which is called Belle Idee which is basically used for psychiatric services to the population. But here we only have the entries for under 24 hours for the two hospitals. These are the first two columns. And then we have the entries of over 24 hours. These are the two following columns. But this is both for accidents. So it is not for illnesses. So it could be a traffic accident or a home accident and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [In English] Now I have some questions to the witness. Will you please have a look on page 24 of your report, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The first paragraph after the table says, if I understand that well, that the difference between the second column and the third column of page 2 -- of table 2, I am sorry, second and third column, is that the all events that occurred outside the siege period or the siege area and such relevant events from outside the indictment period were excluded in the third column?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Okay. Now my question is whether you have the discrimination between those two things, what I mean is the discrimination between events outside the area and outside the date? Because the figures are high. It is more than 2.500 people between the second column and the third one.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: So, do you have the discrimination according to those events excluded because they are outside the date or those are excluded because they are outside the area?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference between the 32.703 and 20.151, the difference are events that are outside the indictment period and indictment area, the area within the confrontation lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes. My question is whether you have the figures for each one of those events excluded, the events excluded because they are outside the area or excluded because they are --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we can provide the statistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: But you don't have it --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right now that I could say immediately how many events were excluded because they are outside the period, outside the area, or both, outside the period and the area. But we can compile the statistics --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: But you have the information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have the information but a query database must be made to show the statistics for killed, wounded and natural deaths. But, generally, if we subtract these two columns in table two, so then we will see the outcome of these exercises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It is total 12.552.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but specific answer to show how many events were excluded because they were outside the indictment period or indictment area or both. I would have to calculate this. I don't have these figures in this report right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I don't know whether we can ask for that, if the Chamber agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If it would be possible for you --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- To introduce--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.
